claims: AsyncConnection and AsyncCursor expose native asyncio counterparts. Same-connection query execution is serialized and all cursors share the same transaction.
Cancellation asks PostgreSQL to cancel the operation, but CancelledError does not prove the operation did not complete. Reconcile uncertain committed writes using stable operation identity.
Connections must be created after process fork, never shared across processes.
Pool connection context commits normally, rolls back on exception, then returns the connection.
Create async pool open=False and explicitly await open/close or use its async context. Constructor-opening is deprecated.
Bound max_size and acquisition timeout; run startup wait to fail promptly rather than deferring connection failure.
COPY participates in normal transaction semantics. Context errors discard COPY input; the outer transaction still controls durable commit.
write_row adapts Python values. Do not combine row-wise adaptation with CSV/DELIMITER/NULL options; preformatted blocks require their own exact format contract.
Binary COPY is type-exact; use set_types when necessary. COPY output lacks complete type information unless supplied.
Pipeline batches protocol round trips; performance depends on latency/workload and is not a universal speed guarantee.
Statement failure aborts the current transaction and skips subsequent queued work until synchronization; PipelineAborted requires rollback/recovery.
executemany uses pipeline internally on supported versions; pipeline mode and COPY are separate primitives.
Ordinary Cursor materializes results client-side. Named ServerCursor retrieves partial results from the server and keeps server resources/transaction open.
A bounded fetchmany/iteration and prompt cursor cleanup are required for bounded retained rows.
Bind data values with %s placeholders and a separate parameter sequence; never interpolate data into SQL text.
SQL identifiers require psycopg.sql.Identifier composition, not value placeholders. Constrain dynamic identifiers to an application allowlist where practical.
Even SELECT starts a transaction by default. End transactions promptly to avoid idle-in-transaction connections.

Connection context commits/rolls back and closes. Connection.transaction on autocommit connection gives explicit top-level transaction ownership; on an already active transaction it may form a savepoint.
Do not pretend nested transaction contexts are independent top-level commits.
Asyncpg is native asyncio and PostgreSQL protocol, with $1 value parameters. Use explicit transaction and pool acquisition scopes.
Default SSL mode is prefer and may fall back. Production must explicitly require verify-full or validating SSLContext; SSL is ignored for Unix sockets.
Bound command_timeout, pool min/max, acquisition timeout, and cursor prefetch.
Connection.transaction provides explicit transactions. create_pool is the native pooling API.
Independent tasks acquire independent connections; a single asyncpg connection is not a shared parallel execution lane.
Cursor iteration requires an explicit transaction.
PgBouncer prepared statement behavior is deployment-dependent; disabling statement_cache_size can be necessary. Do not claim every pooler/version supports prepared statements.
Use explicit postgresql+psycopg URLs for both create_engine and create_async_engine. The constructor selects sync/async.
Use SQLAlchemy URL.create for structured credentials and connect_args for TLS/timeouts. Avoid layering a second pool unless deliberately configured.
engine.begin manages both connection and transaction, committing normal exit and rolling back exceptions.
engine.connect alone is not a commit context. Autobegun writes must be explicitly committed or use engine.begin.
yield_per/stream_results configure server-side result streaming; close result and connection when stopping early.
AsyncSession is mutable transaction state and must not be shared by concurrent tasks.
Use independent session contexts and avoid implicit lazy I/O in async code; explicit async execution/streaming and eager load decisions make I/O ownership visible.
Dispose async engine at shutdown; connection/session cleanup must survive exceptions.
Separate table models from create/public data models. Construct persistence model from explicitly validated input.
SQLModel uses SQLAlchemy; therefore PostgreSQL driver and transaction semantics still apply.
Table-model constructor semantics differ from ordinary DTO validation; docs call for model_validate when validation is needed.
Use a separate strict Pydantic input contract and timezone-aware PostgreSQL column; do not assume ORM declaration alone proves boundary validation.
iter_batches=True yields DataFrames but may still materialize the full driver result unless the driver is configured for streaming.
With SQLAlchemy use stream_results=True and explicit batch_size. A backend may ignore requested batch sizes.
For the narrow reference, use a psycopg server cursor, bounded fetchmany, and explicit DataFrame schema; memory contract also needs a maximum row/payload size.
Default validation may coerce values. strict=True rejects type coercion for Python input; JSON input has some permitted string representations.
Use model_validate on the declared boundary; add explicit tests for booleans-as-integers, nonfinite floats, oversized strings/bodies, unknown fields, and malformed JSON.
extra=forbid rejects undeclared fields. frozen prevents assignment and may make a model hashable.
Frozen is faux-immutability: nested mutable containers are not a deep immutable authorization snapshot. Use immutable field types or recursively freeze copied data.
pyrsistent supplies immutable/persistent functional collections (PMap, PRecord, PVector). Persistent here describes retained versions, not disk or database durability.
Use freeze or immutable nested values for snapshots. Store durable checkpoint/effect data in PostgreSQL, not only a PMap.
verify-full validates both trusted certificate chain and host name. require does not express equivalent host identity validation.
Local test transport and production transport must be explicit separate profiles; a local non-TLS PG-wire run cannot prove production certificate verification.
LIMIT requires a unique ORDER BY for predictable subsets.
Use monotonic unique keyset cursor (id > last_id ORDER BY id LIMIT bound) or composite immutable ordering with unique tiebreaker.
If a stable multi-page snapshot is required, keep REPEATABLE READ read-only transaction; high-water id alone does not isolate updates/deletes.
READ COMMITTED ordered locking reads may observe updated ordering values after waiting; use immutable ordering for queue/keyset paths.
Authority check/use must use a single transaction with a locked grant or atomic guarded mutation. Independent preflight authorization is insufficient.
Observed current stable release v0.7.0 published 2026-09-20. Linux amd64 tar.gz asset digest is recorded separately.
Go library is github.com/tailscale/tailcat. It is not a native Python package; a pinned CLI provides a narrow standalone Python integration seam.
Tailcat uses WireGuard data-plane connections without Tailscale control-plane account configuration; address data is exchanged out of band.
Use --allow with explicit client node keys; an unrestricted address is a capability secret. Keep PSK enabled.
forward binds loopback by default. Port forwarding does not automatically pass tunnel peer identity to PostgreSQL.
tailcat serve --allow=nodekey:<key> exec -- <command> runs a fixed command per connection.
Spawned command receives TAILCAT_PEER_KEY and TAILCAT_REMOTE_ADDR from tunnel context.
Use argv lists without shell=True. Worker obtains peer only from trusted launcher environment, rejects any client-provided peer override, and validates key grammar.
Upstream TestLocalDERPMode sets TS_DEBUG_TAILCAT_LOCAL_DERP=1 and TAILCAT_ADDR_FILE on the server.
Both server and client use --derpmap-url=none; server embeds local relay in generated address, enabling live hermetic encrypted transport tests without public DERP.
Keep this upstream debug mode isolated to test profile; it is not a production relay configuration.
Upstream live exec test generates a client key, starts serve exec, round-trips bytes, and checks TAILCAT_PEER_KEY.
This can be adapted to a fixed Python worker over stdin/stdout with bounded framing and PostgreSQL grant checks; no FastAPI layer is required.

recommended_primitives.contract: Bounded connection/pool lifecycle with explicit production verify-full and isolated local-test profile.
Synchronous and asynchronous parameter-bound raw SQL, explicit transaction ownership, no shared task connection.
Atomic Psycopg COPY row ingestion and separate pipeline reference; no universal speed claim.
falsifiers: one pipeline statement fails => whole transaction no effects

recommended_primitives.contract: Unique immutable keyset ordering, explicit batch cap and end boundary.
falsifiers: multi-page no duplicates or gaps in fixture
mutation of ordering disallowed or stated

recommended_primitives.contract: SQLAlchemy explicit postgresql+psycopg sync/async engine and SQLModel with separate input DTO.
Bounded cursor batches parsed into strict DTO and Polars with explicit schema.
Tailcat-authenticated peer from trusted launcher; PG live authority + epoch check and effect/outbox mutation in one transaction.
falsifiers: local env spoof excluded by containment boundary

recommended_primitives.contract: PG authoritative effect+outbox atomicity, Redis delivery at least once, durable consumer checkpoint/idempotency before ACK.
Content-defined chunks persist hash/sequence/length with strict total size bounds, repeatable boundaries and resumable checkpoint.
falsifiers: same content different network read segmentation

draft_corrections: Replace hardcoded superuser/password DSNs with configuration and least-privilege runtime role.
Do not rank asyncpg universally faster; benchmark actual payload, transaction, concurrency, and latency profiles.
Psycopg2 has legacy asynchronous/polling capability; say it lacks Psycopg3 native asyncio API rather than all async support.
psycopg[binary] bundles compiled dependencies; plain psycopg can use system libpq. Binary option is packaging choice, not absence of libpq.
Pin drivers and extras explicitly; do not add FastAPI, Kubernetes, or a second database engine merely because baseline tools mention them.
Use explicit projection rather than SELECT *, stable order when fetching one row, and explicit row absence behavior.
Use try/finally or async connection context for asyncpg closure, explicit transaction scope for multi-statement effects.
SQLAlchemy connection context alone does not commit application writes.
